extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, coeditors, and editors submitting to or handling manuscripts for AER: Insights (economics journal)
extracted.subtask_short: AER Insights submission and review policy
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial and peer-review standards, procedural rules, and policy requirements for submitting, reviewing, and publishing manuscripts in the American Economic Review: Insights. Covers review model, editorial assignment, conflicts of interest, decisions, data/code/legality requirements, comments/replies, disclosures, AI use, and RCT registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model (single‑blind)
rubrics_metrics.description: All manuscripts submitted to American Economic Review: Insights undergo single-blind peer review—the name of the author is revealed to the referee(s), while the referee(s) remain anonymous to authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a manuscript is received, the editor assigns it to a coeditor or to themselves (in the role of coeditor) to oversee the review process and to make a publication decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coeditor assignment criteria and author requests
rubrics_metrics.description: During submission, authors have the opportunity to request one or more specific coeditors to handle their paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor usually follows such requests if they are consistent with the criteria for assigning papers, including field of expertise of the coeditor, equalization of workload, and adherence to conflict-of-interest rules. Once assigned, papers are handled by the designated coeditor throughout the decision process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor/coeditor right to return without referee review (desk rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor and coeditors reserve the right to return manuscripts to authors without referee review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision to return a manuscript without review is based on several considerations, including expected probability of meeting the standards of AER: Insights, breadth of topic, and interest to the AER: Insights audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision categories (reject or conditional accept); no revise-and-resubmit
rubrics_metrics.description: First decisions on manuscripts that have been sent to reviewers are either 'reject' or 'conditional accept.' AER: Insights does not have a traditional revise-and-resubmit category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not expect a standard R&R; conditional acceptance is the mechanism for requiring changes prior to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional acceptance requirements and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditional acceptance means that AER: Insights expects to publish the paper subject to changes detailed in the coeditor's decision letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are typically given an 8-week deadline to return the revised manuscript. The conditions may include revisions to exposition, analysis, and/or presentation of results, and they are expected to be achievable without substantial uncertainty. When a conditionally accepted manuscript is resubmitted, the coeditor typically makes a final decision without returning the manuscript to the referees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final compliance checks (data/code & legality)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the final stage of the review process, the paper undergoes a check to determine whether it complies with the AEA's Data and Code Availability Policy and Data Legality Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with those policies is required prior to publication; see linked full policies for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of handling coeditor in publication
rubrics_metrics.description: When papers are accepted and published, the coeditor in charge is identified in the acknowledgement footnote of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identification applies to accepted papers; guest editors are also named in the acknowledgement when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest: mandatory recusal categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Coeditors are recused from papers involving current colleagues at the same institution (regardless of department), as well as graduate students at the same institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional recusal grounds spelled out by policy include: coauthors of current papers or papers published less than two years ago; untenured students that they advised; a coeditor at a different journal who is currently handling one of the coeditor’s own papers or has accepted one of the coeditor’s own papers in the past two years; and family members. Coeditors must disclose any other close personal or professional relationship which, in their opinion, creates a conflict (e.g., coauthor of a current project, former tenured student that the coeditor is still close to, advisee of author, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict identification and handling procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the responsibility of the coeditor to identify a conflict of interest to the editor. In addition, authors are asked during the submission process whether they are aware of any coeditor who has a conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a conflict is identified, the paper will be assigned to a different coeditor with appropriate procedures for confidentiality of refereeing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling submissions from coeditors or the editor (guest editor procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted by a coeditor or the editor are handled by a guest editor employing appropriate confidentiality procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guest editor has full editorial discretion. If the paper is submitted by a coeditor, the editor invites a guest editor. If the paper is submitted by the editor, the coeditors jointly decide on the guest editor. If possible, the guest editor is drawn from former editors or coeditors of AEA journals or from members of the board of editors. The guest editor's name is identified in the acknowledgement footnote of the published article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for Comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments submitted to AER: Insights should provide a substantial and general-interest contribution beyond what could be known from the original article and other articles in the literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may be summarily rejected by the editor or the assigned coeditor or sent for review to the author of the original article and likely to other reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for Replies
rubrics_metrics.description: If the author of the original paper submits a Reply, it will be sent to the author of the Comment and generally to other reviewers. There is no automatic right to Reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the Reply to be accepted for publication, it must provide substantive and material discussion of the issues in question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online alternatives for comments that do not meet formal publication standard
rubrics_metrics.description: For comments that do not meet the standard for formal publication, the coeditor may, depending on the substance and merit of the comment, the reaction of the authors of the article being commented on, and possibly the advice of reviewers, provide an option for the comment to be posted on the article’s landing page under 'Additional Materials.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The terms 'e-comment,' 'e-reply,' and 'e-amendment' (a cooperative document between the authors of the comment and the authors of the original publication) will be used for online postings to ensure that they are clearly distinguished from formal publications in the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of items in the journal (lead article selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: The order in which papers appear in each issue is determined by the editor in consultation with the coeditors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper that appears first (the 'lead article') is one that the editor particularly wants to call attention to, based on factors such as the importance of the questions it addresses, the quality of analysis, the innovation over the literature, and the clarity of presentation. The order of the subsequent articles generally follows the order in which the articles were accepted, though sometimes there are deviations (e.g., to group related articles together). Any comments and replies are printed after regular articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure statements requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting papers for peer review, all authors must provide disclosure statements identifying potential conflicts of interest. If authors have nothing to disclose, they are obligated to submit a statement explicitly stating this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure statements should also disclose whether IRB approval was obtained for the project, and if not, state the reason(s). For published papers, a brief summary of potential conflicts of interest should appear in the acknowledgement footnote. The entire disclosure statement is posted with the paper on the journal's website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of artificial intelligence (AI) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) software, such as chatbots or other large language models, may not be listed as an author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If AI software was used in the preparation of the manuscript, including drafting or editing text, this must be briefly described during the submission process. Authors are solely accountable for, and must thoroughly fact-check, outputs created with the help of AI software. The reviewer's report is expected to reflect their own careful reading and evaluation of the paper. Any use of AI during the review must be disclosed in the reviewer's cover letter and must be limited to tools that guarantee that the manuscript will not be used for training AI models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Legality Policy (legal acquisition of data)
rubrics_metrics.description: All data used in papers published in journals of the American Economic Association should be legally acquired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The coeditor in charge may reject the paper if some or all of the data were not legally obtained. See the full Data Legality Policy (effective July 2023).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Code Availability Policy (replicability requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to acceptance, authors of papers that contain empirical work, simulations, or experimental work must provide the data, code, and other details of the computations sufficient to permit replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should follow the full Data and Code Availability Policy linked by the journal for specific formatting, timing, and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCT registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the policy of the AEA journals that all work involving field experiments must be registered with the AEA RCT Registry prior to submission for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors conducting field experiments must register in advance; see the AEA RCT Registry for registration procedures and required information.
